scenarios.title: The first frame is auth, and a request made before it succeeds is held until it does
scenarios.why: The server reads the first frame on a socket as the handshake, so a request written first would be consumed as one.

scenarios.title: An uncorrelated auth.expired re-authenticates once per episode, without reconnecting
scenarios.why: A second lapse notice in the same episode must not start a second re-auth, and recovery never needs a new socket.

scenarios.title: A request made during an expiry episode is written after the re-auth succeeds
scenarios.why: The server refuses everything but auth while a session is expired.

scenarios.title: An auth.expired that names a request expires the session and resends that request alone
scenarios.why: A client that is actively sending sees only correlated notices. The request accepted before the lapse has its reply replayed, so resending it would duplicate it.

scenarios.title: An announced expiry resends nothing the server did not name
scenarios.why: Without a named refusal, every in-flight request was accepted before the lapse; resending any of them duplicates it.

scenarios.title: auth.expired.dropped resends each named request immediately, and nothing else
scenarios.why: The report arrives after the auth.success that ended the episode, so a binding that only re-queues loses exactly the requests it exists to save.

scenarios.title: A truncated report makes every unanswered request suspect, each resent once and answered ones never
scenarios.why: A truncated list is a sample, so the only safe policy is the blind one, but a request already answered is not in flight.

scenarios.title: A report naming no request and not truncated is complete: only events were lost
scenarios.why: An event answers no request, so a report of only lost events leaves nothing to resend.

scenarios.title: A replayed auth.success on an authenticated session changes nothing and rewrites nothing
scenarios.why: A server that parks outbound frames replays the handshake reply after the re-auth that released it.

scenarios.title: auth.failure on a live socket is handed to the caller, and no further re-auth is attempted
scenarios.why: Re-authenticating the same credential on the socket that refused it would be refused again and would hide the failure from its owner. Any retry belongs to the owner on a fresh socket (RetryFreshSocket for invalid_token and unauthorized, per ADR 0041), which this socket never sees.

scenarios.title: A code minted after this build is forwarded as received and costs the session nothing
scenarios.why: A shipped game cannot be updated, so a code it does not know must be carried, not rejected.

scenarios.title: A frame type minted after this build is delivered, and the session stays usable
scenarios.why: The server may add an event type at any time; a client that treats it as a protocol error breaks every shipped game at once.

steps.call: The caller sends a frame of `type`, with an optional `payload`, through the SDK.
steps.expectDelivered: A frame of `type` has been handed to the caller since the previous expectDelivered, with `error` as its code when given.
steps.expectQuiet: The SDK has written nothing that an expectSent has not consumed.
steps.expectSent: The next frame the SDK wrote has `type`. `bind` names an alias for its requestId; `same` asserts its requestId equals the one bound to that alias.
steps.expectState: The SDK session is in `state`: pending, authenticated, expired, or closed.
steps.open: The transport becomes writable and the SDK starts its session.
steps.serve: The scripted server delivers `frame` to the SDK. Every object {"ref": alias} inside it is replaced by the request id bound to that alias.
